dataNotes: Two Trek-published documents: Trek's Roscoe consumer FAQ PDF and Trek's 2022 Roscoe service manual. STATED verbatim: 'Boost148 rear thru axle ... ISCG 05 mount ... and UDH (universal derailleur hanger)'; 'Boost110 front, Boost 148 rear'; 'maximum tire size? 29x2.6" (XS: 27.5x2.6")'; 'Is it compatible with other wheel/tire sizes? No.'; 'BSA 73 (threaded)'; '52mm chainline 32T; 55mm chainline 34T'; '160mm direct mount on all sizes. Adaptable to 180mm'; 'up to 150mm of fork travel'; '430mm stays'; seat tube inside diameter 31.6mm; 'This bicycle frame is designed to use a Universal Derailleur Hanger (UDH)' with 'thru axle must be M12x1.0 with a 12.7mm thread'. maxTyreWidthMm 66 = 2.6in (Trek itself prints 66.04mm for 2.6in in the Gen 4 manual). LEFT NULL: headsetTaper (never stated in either document); bottleMounts (FAQ says all sizes fit a bottle, no count). hasEyelets false - FAQ: 'ISCG 05 mounts for a chain guide or bash guard and none of that other stuff'. wheelDiameter ISO_622 covers S-XL; XS is 27.5in. EXCLUDED from bikes: Roscoe 6 - Trek's FAQ explicitly says it 'utilizes a carry-forward frame'. Roscoe Gen 4 (2026) dropped entirely as a platform: its service manual never states a bottom bracket standard.

Trek's '2024 Procaliber Alloy' service manual. STATED verbatim: 'Rear O.L.D 148mm'; 'Maximum tire size 29" x 2.4"'; 'Bottom bracket BSA 73'; 'Rear brake mount Minimum: 160mm / Maximum: 180mm with adapter'; 'Chainline 52mm max chainring 30T, 55mm max chainring 34T'; 'Seat tube inside diameter: 31.6mm'; fork 'Recommended 120 / Maximum 130'; section heading 'Rear axle and UDH' with 'Thru axle, 12x180mm'. maxTyreWidthMm 61 = 2.4in. LEFT NULL: headsetTaper, iscgStandard, chainstayLengthMm, bottleMounts, hasEyelets - none stated anywhere in the manual. mulletApproved false is DERIVED from the manual listing only a 29in tyre size with no alternative wheel configuration. MODEL-YEAR NOTE: the 2024 alloy Procaliber is BSA 73 while the 2025 carbon is press-fit BB92 - genuinely different frames, split accordingly.

MODEL-YEAR TRAP HANDLED: the 2025 carbon Procaliber is a NEW generation that drops the IsoSpeed decoupler for the 'IsoBow' seatstay junction. The pre-2025 carbon Procaliber is a DIFFERENT frame and is NOT covered here. Trek's '2025 Procaliber Carbon' service manual, STATED verbatim: 'Rear O.L.D. 148 mm'; 'Maximum tire size 29" x 2.4"'; 'Bottom bracket Press-fit BB92'; 'Rear brake mount Minimum: 160 mm / Maximum: 180 mm with adapter'; 'Chainline 55 mm, Chainring Min 30T Max 38T round'; 'Seat tube inner diameter: 31.6 mm'; fork 'Min 110 mm / Max (recommended) 120 mm'; 'Thru axle, 12 x 180 mm'. hangerStandard LEFT NULL deliberately: this manual's section is titled 'Rear axle and derailleur', NOT 'Rear axle and UDH' as the alloy manual is, and never uses the words 'Universal Derailleur Hanger' - even though it shows a direct-mount SRAM Transmission option. Not asserting UDH without Trek saying it. Also null: headsetTaper, iscgStandard, chainstayLengthMm, bottleMounts, hasEyelets. Trim list comes from launch press coverage rather than a Trek spec page, hence medium confidence overall; the frame numbers themselves are from Trek's own manual.

Trek's 'Top Fuel - Gen 4' (MY25) service manual plus Trek's Top Fuel Gen 4 FAQ. STATED verbatim in the manual: 'Rear O.L.D 148 mm'; 'Rear brake mount 180 mm direct post mount, adaptable to 203 mm'; 'Maximum tire size M, ML, L, XL: 29" x 2.5"; S: 27.5" x 2.5"'; 'Bottom bracket BSA73'; fork maximum 140mm; 'Seatpost outer diameter: 34.9 mm'; 'Chainline 55 mm only, Chainring Minimum 30T Maximum 34T round / 32T oval'; 'Headset Upper: 41 mm Lower: 52 mm'; shock 'Eye-to-eye length: 185 mm / Stroke length: 50 mm (55 mm max) / Upper mount: 54 mm x 10 mm (trunnion) / Lower mount: 30 mm x 8 mm'; section heading 'Active Braking Pivot with Universal Derailleur Hanger' with 'Thru axle, 12 X 184.5 mm'. STATED in the FAQ: 'ALL sizes have 1 water bottle mount'; 'M and larger can be set up with a 27.5" rear wheel with the bike in the high Mino position and a fork with 140mm of travel' (hence mulletApproved true). headsetTaper DERIVED from the stated 41mm upper / 52mm lower bores, which are the standard IS41/IS52 sizes for a 1.5-to-1.125 tapered steerer. shockStrokeMm 50 is stock; 55mm is Trek's stated maximum. maxTyreWidthMm 64 = 2.5in. LEFT NULL: iscgStandard (never mentioned), chainstayLengthMm (size-specific, no numbers given). hasEyelets false - the FAQ describes an under-top-tube accessory point but no rack/fender/kickstand mounts. wheelDiameter ISO_622 covers M-XL; size S is 27.5in only.

Same Trek 'Top Fuel - Gen 4' (MY25) service manual, which explicitly covers both carbon and alloy frames (parts marked 'Carbon frames only', separate alloy routing diagrams, and a carbon/alloy split in the seatpost insertion table). Every specification field here is STATED verbatim in that single specifications table and applies to both materials - see the carbon entry for the verbatim quotes. The only stated carbon/alloy difference is maximum seatpost insertion (carbon S 240mm vs alloy S 230mm), which is not a field in this schema. headsetTaper DERIVED from the stated 41mm/52mm headset bores. LEFT NULL: iscgStandard, chainstayLengthMm. Separate platform entry only because platforms are grouped by (family, material, suspension).

Trek's '2023 Fuel EX' service manual (Gen 6) and Trek's own MY23 Fuel EX FAQ PDF. STATED verbatim in the manual: 'Rear brake mount Minimum 180mm, direct mount / Maximum Adaptable to 203mm'; 'Maximum tire size - 29" wheel set: 29" x 2.5"; 27.5" (XS and S frame): 27.5" x 2.5"'; 'Bottom bracket BSA 73 / ISCG tabs ISCG 05, 3 bolt'; 'Seat tube inside diameter 34.9'; fork maximum 160mm on 29in sizes; 'Chainline (1x only) 55mm, Chainring Minimum 28T Maximum Round: 34T Oval: 32T'; shock 'Eye-to Eye-length: 185mm / Stroke length: 55mm / Upper width: 54mm x 10mm / Lower width: 40mm x 8mm'; and 'This bicycle frame is designed to use a Universal Derailleur Hanger (UDH)'. STATED in the FAQ: 'this bike is mullet compatible'; one bottle per size; 'Fuel EX is a purpose-built trail bike and doesn't have mounts for a kickstand, racks, or fenders' (hasEyelets false); 'takes a 185mm x 55mm shock with an industry standard 54mm x 10mm upper Trunnion and 40mm x 8mm lower standard pin mount'. WEAKEST FIELD - rearAxleType: neither Trek document states the rear O.L.D. numerically. 148mm Boost comes from Trek's published component spec string for Gen 6 completes as mirrored on retailer listings, not from a Trek page rendered directly. It is consistent with the UDH M12x1.0 requirement, but it is corroboration-grade, not primary - hence medium confidence. LEFT NULL: headsetTaper (angle-adjustable headset, no bore sizes published), chainstayLengthMm (size-specific, no numbers). maxTyreWidthMm 64 = 2.5in. wheelDiameter ISO_622 covers S-XXL; XS is 27.5in only.

Same Trek '2023 Fuel EX' service manual, which covers carbon and aluminium frames together (separate 'Frame guards - aluminum frame' section, carbon/aluminium columns in the seatpost table, and carbon/aluminium part numbers for chainstay, seatstay and rocker). All specification values quoted in the carbon entry apply to both materials. The only STATED material differences are maximum seatpost insertion (alloy 25-30mm shorter per size, and XXL exists only in aluminium) and maximum fork travel on the 27.5 sizes (alloy XS/S max 150mm / 550mm A2C vs carbon 560mm; both 160mm on 29in sizes). maxForkTravelMm 160 recorded here applies to the 29in sizes. Same caveat as the carbon entry: rearAxleType 148 Boost is corroboration-grade, not stated numerically in the Trek documents read - hence medium confidence. LEFT NULL: headsetTaper, chainstayLengthMm.

Trek's 'Slash Alloy and Carbon - Gen 6' (MY24) service manual and Trek's Slash Gen 6 FAQ. STATED verbatim in the manual: 'Rear O.L.D 148mm'; 'Rear brake mount 200mm direct post mount, adaptable to 220mm' (with a notice that a 203mm rotor needs RockShox 1.5mm adapter spacers); 'Maximum tire size M, ML, L, XL: 29" x 2.5"; S: 27.5" x 2.5"'; 'Bottom bracket BSA73'; fork maximum 190mm; 'Chainline 55, Chainring Minimum 28T Maximum 34T round / 32T oval'; 'Seat tube inside diameter: 34.9mm'; shock 'Eye-to Eye-length: 230mm / Stroke length: 65mm / air can mount 54mmx10mm / shaft mount 20mmx8mm'; section 'Active Braking Pivot with Universal Derailleur Hanger' with 'Thru axle, M12x167.35mm'. STATED in the FAQ: 'ISCG 05, 3-bolt'; 'Stock mixed-wheel builds (29" front, 27.5" rear) on all sizes except S'; 'size M and up can run a 29" rear wheel' with a swapped lower shock mount. IMPORTANT: rearBrakeMountType recorded as generic POST_MOUNT because the enum has no 200mm post-mount value - the frame's native mount is a 200mm direct post mount (220mm max). Do NOT read this as a 160/180 mount. shockMountType TRUNNION is DERIVED: the manual gives the upper mount as 54mm x 10mm without naming it, and Trek's own Fuel EX FAQ calls that identical interface a 'Trunnion' mount. LEFT NULL: headsetTaper (angle-adjustable headset, no bore sizes), chainstayLengthMm (size-specific via BB shell position), hasEyelets (Trek states nothing either way; the frame does carry an integrated rear mudguard on 27.5 builds). bottleMounts 1 DERIVED from the FAQ's 'All models come with a Bontrager right side load water bottle cage'.

Same Trek 'Slash Alloy and Carbon - Gen 6' service manual, which documents both materials (separate alloy routing and alloy frame-guard sections, and separate carbon/alloy chainstay part numbers 46192/46193). Every specification-table value is shared with the carbon frame - see the carbon entry for verbatim quotes. The only STATED material difference is maximum seatpost insertion on size Small (carbon 290mm, alloy 295mm). Trek's FAQ notes alloy and carbon stays 'will fit' each other but were not tested, so Trek does not officially recommend mixing them. LEFT NULL for the same reasons: headsetTaper, chainstayLengthMm, hasEyelets. rearBrakeMountType is generic POST_MOUNT because the frame's native 200mm direct post mount (220mm max) has no matching enum value.
